title: Wave 12: Remaining Sources Deep Mine (Nepos, Eutropius, Aurelius Victor, Curtius Rufus, Xenophon, Harivamsha, Shahnameh, Abdias, Africanus, Sayce & L.W. King)

nodes.name: Aristides 'the Just' of Athens
nodes.role: Athenian Archon, Strategos & Delian League Assessor
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
nodes.notes: Athenian statesman famed in Cornelius Nepos for incorruptibility in assessing Delian League tribute alongside Themistocles.

nodes.name: Regent Pausanias of Sparta
nodes.role: Agiad Spartan Regent & Victor of Plataea
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
nodes.notes: Commanded the allied Greek forces at Plataea (479 BCE); Nepos pairs his triumph and subsequent Byzantine intrigue.

nodes.name: Thrasybulus of Steiria
nodes.role: Athenian Strategos & Restorer of Democracy
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
nodes.notes: Led the overthrow of the Thirty Tyrants at Athens; celebrated in Nepos's gallery of civic liberators.

nodes.name: Conon & Timotheus of Athens
nodes.role: Father-Son Athenian Admirals & Commanders
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
nodes.notes: Conon won Cnidus (394 BCE) rebuilding Athens' Long Walls; his son Timotheus secured the Second Athenian League.

nodes.name: Iphicrates & Chabrias of Athens
nodes.role: Peltast Tacticians & Commanders in Thrace and Egypt
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
nodes.notes: Iphicrates wed King Cotys I's Thracian daughter; Chabrias commanded Pharaoh Nectanebo II's forces in Egypt.

nodes.name: Satrap Datames of Cappadocia
nodes.role: Carian-Scythian Satrap & Ruler of Cappadocia
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
nodes.notes: Nepos praises Datames, son of Camissares and a Scythian mother, as the ablest non-Greek general of his age.

nodes.name: Pelopidas of Thebes
nodes.role: Theban Boeotarch & Leader of the Sacred Band
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
nodes.notes: Co-architect of the Theban Hegemony with Epaminondas; fell victorious at Cynoscephalae.

nodes.name: King Agesilaus II of Sparta
nodes.role: Eurypontid King of Sparta & Egyptian Campaign Ally
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
Xenophon, Expedition of Cyrus & Ten Thousand (1776)
nodes.notes: Propelled to the Spartan throne by Lysander; campaigned across Asia Minor and Egypt until age 84.

nodes.name: Dion of Syracuse
nodes.role: Ruler of Syracuse & Brother-in-Law of Dionysius I
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
nodes.notes: Overthrew Dionysius II of Syracuse with Plato's circle; detailed in Nepos's biography.

nodes.name: Timoleon of Corinth
nodes.role: Liberator of Sicily & Victor at the Crimissus
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
nodes.notes: Sent from Corinth to expel Carthaginian and tyrannical rule across Sicily, restoring civic constitutions.

nodes.name: Phocion 'the Good' & Titus Pomponius Atticus
nodes.role: Athenian Strategos & Roman-Athenian Bridge Biographer
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
nodes.notes: Nepos pairs incorruptible Phocion with Titus Pomponius Atticus, Cicero's correspondent and Roman genealogist.

nodes.name: Xenophon of Erchia (Ten Thousand)
nodes.role: Athenian General, Socratic Historian & Author of Anabasis
sources: Xenophon, Expedition of Cyrus & Ten Thousand (1776)
nodes.notes: Elected general after Cunaxa (401 BCE) to lead the Ten Thousand Greeks from Babylonia to the Black Sea.

nodes.name: Clearchus of Sparta & Proxenus of Boeotia
nodes.role: Mercenary Commanders of Cyrus the Younger
sources: Xenophon, Expedition of Cyrus & Ten Thousand (1776)
nodes.notes: Recruited Greek hoplite regiments for Cyrus's march to Cunaxa; betrayed and executed by Tissaphernes.

nodes.name: King Seuthes II of Odrysian Thrace
nodes.role: Odrysian King of Thrace & Ally of the Ten Thousand
sources: Xenophon, Expedition of Cyrus & Ten Thousand (1776)
nodes.notes: Reclaimed ancestral coastal Thrace with Xenophon's returning Ten Thousand mercenaries in 400/399 BCE.

nodes.name: Hamilcar Barca of Carthage
nodes.role: Carthaginian General, Ruler of Iberia & Father of Hannibal
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
nodes.notes: Founder of Barcid Iberia and father of Hannibal, Hasdrubal, and Mago; administered oath of enmity to Hannibal.

nodes.name: Hasdrubal & Mago Barca
nodes.role: Barcid Commanders in Spain, Metaurus & Liguria
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
Eutropius, Abridgment of Roman History (Watson 1853)
Aurelius Victor, Lives of the Illustrious Romans (1693)
Florus, Roman History (1675)
nodes.notes: Brothers of Hannibal who sustained the Carthaginian two-front campaigns in Hispania and northern Italy.

nodes.name: Marcus Porcius Cato 'the Elder'
nodes.role: Roman Censor, Historian & Jurist
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
Eutropius, Abridgment of Roman History (Watson 1853)
Aurelius Victor, Lives of the Illustrious Romans (1693)
Florus, Roman History (1675)
nodes.notes: First Latin prose historian (Origines); Nepos composed a dedicated life of Cato as moral exemplar.

nodes.name: Scipio Aemilianus Africanus Minor
nodes.role: Roman Consul, Conqueror of Carthage (146 BCE) & Numantia
sources: Eutropius, Abridgment of Roman History (Watson 1853)
Aurelius Victor, Lives of the Illustrious Romans (1693)
Florus, Roman History (1675)
nodes.notes: Adopted grandson of Scipio Africanus and biological son of Aemilius Paullus; ended the Third Punic War.

nodes.name: Tiberius & Gaius Gracchus
nodes.role: Tribunes of the Plebs & Grandsons of Scipio Africanus
sources: Eutropius, Abridgment of Roman History (Watson 1853)
Aurelius Victor, Lives of the Illustrious Romans (1693)
Florus, Roman History (1675)
nodes.notes: Sons of Cornelia Africana whose agrarian and civic reforms opened the Late Roman Republic crises in Florus.

nodes.name: Gaius Marius (Seven-Time Consul)
nodes.role: Reformer of Roman Legions & Uncle-by-Marriage to Julius Caesar
sources: Eutropius, Abridgment of Roman History (Watson 1853)
Aurelius Victor, Lives of the Illustrious Romans (1693)
Florus, Roman History (1675)
nodes.notes: Married Julia, aunt of Julius Caesar; defeated Jugurtha, the Teutones, and the Cimbri.

nodes.name: Lucius Cornelius Sulla Felix
nodes.role: Roman Dictator & Opponent of Mithridates VI and Marius
sources: Eutropius, Abridgment of Roman History (Watson 1853)
Aurelius Victor, Lives of the Illustrious Romans (1693)
Florus, Roman History (1675)
nodes.notes: First Roman general to march on Rome; his constitutional settlements and civil wars dominate Eutropius Book V.

nodes.name: Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus (Pompey)
nodes.role: Roman Triumvir, Conqueror of the East & Son-in-Law of Caesar
sources: Eutropius, Abridgment of Roman History (Watson 1853)
Aurelius Victor, Lives of the Illustrious Romans (1693)
Florus, Roman History (1675)
nodes.notes: Wed Julia Caesaris; reorganized Syria, Pontus, and Judea (63 BCE) before Pharsalus.

nodes.name: Emperors Titus & Domitian (Flavian Sons)
nodes.role: Flavian Roman Emperors (79 - 96 CE)
sources: Eutropius, Abridgment of Roman History (Watson 1853)
Aurelius Victor, Lives of the Illustrious Romans (1693)
Florus, Roman History (1675)
nodes.notes: Sons of Vespasian profiled in Aurelius Victor and Eutropius for Jerusalem, Pompeii relief, and Danubian wars.

nodes.name: Emperors Nerva, Antoninus Pius & Marcus Aurelius
nodes.role: Adoptive Nerva-Antonine Roman Emperors (96 - 180 CE)
sources: Eutropius, Abridgment of Roman History (Watson 1853)
Aurelius Victor, Lives of the Illustrious Romans (1693)
Florus, Roman History (1675)
nodes.notes: Adoptive imperial succession linking Trajan and Hadrian down to philosopher-emperor Marcus Aurelius.

nodes.name: Emperors Probus, Carus & Constantius I Chlorus
nodes.role: Illyrian Roman Emperors & Father of Constantine I
sources: Eutropius, Abridgment of Roman History (Watson 1853)
Aurelius Victor, Lives of the Illustrious Romans (1693)
Florus, Roman History (1675)
nodes.notes: Restored the Rhine-Danube frontier between Aurelian, Diocletian, and Constantine I in Eutropius Book IX.

nodes.name: Hephaestion son of Amyntor
nodes.role: Chiliarch & Second-in-Command to Alexander the Great
sources: Quintus Curtius Rufus, History of Alexander the Great
nodes.notes: Lifelong companion of Alexander; wed Drypetis, daughter of Darius III, in the Susa weddings (324 BCE).

nodes.name: Parmenion & Philotas of Macedon
nodes.role: Senior Marshal & Companion Cavalry Commander
sources: Quintus Curtius Rufus, History of Alexander the Great
nodes.notes: Anchored Alexander's left flank at Granicus, Issus, and Gaugamela; purged in Drangiana in Curtius Rufus Book VI.

nodes.name: Cleitus 'the Black' & Craterus
nodes.role: Macedonian Marshals & Guardian of the Royal House
sources: Quintus Curtius Rufus, History of Alexander the Great
Henry Fynes Clinton, Fasti Hellenici Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Cleitus saved Alexander at Granicus; Craterus co-commanded the Macedonian homeland with Antipater.

nodes.name: Queen Roxana of Bactria & King Alexander IV
nodes.role: Queen Consort of Alexander the Great & King of Macedon
sources: Quintus Curtius Rufus, History of Alexander the Great
Henry Fynes Clinton, Fasti Hellenici Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Daughter of Oxyartes of Sogdiana; bore Alexander IV, last Argead king of the united empire.

nodes.name: Queen Stateira II & Queen Mother Sisygambis
nodes.role: Achaemenid Queen Consort of Alexander & Mother of Darius III
sources: Quintus Curtius Rufus, History of Alexander the Great
nodes.notes: Curtius Rufus records Alexander's chivalrous adoption of Sisygambis as mother and marriage to Stateira II at Susa.

nodes.name: King Bessus (Artaxerxes V) & Spitamenes of Sogdiana
nodes.role: Satrap of Bactria & Sogdian Resistance Leader
sources: Quintus Curtius Rufus, History of Alexander the Great
nodes.notes: Bessus claimed the Achaemenid diadem; Spitamenes's daughter Apama later married Seleucus I, founding the Seleucid line.

nodes.name: King Porus (Purushottama) & King Taxiles (Ambhi)
nodes.role: Monarchs of Paurava (Jhelum) & Taxila
sources: Quintus Curtius Rufus, History of Alexander the Great
nodes.notes: Met Alexander across the Hydaspes (326 BCE) in Curtius Rufus Book VIII; Porus confirmed as sovereign of Punjab.

nodes.name: Perdiccas the Regent (Chiliarch of Babylon)
nodes.role: First Regent of Alexander's Empire (323 - 320 BCE)
sources: Quintus Curtius Rufus, History of Alexander the Great
Henry Fynes Clinton, Fasti Hellenici Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Received Alexander's signet ring at Babylon; led the coalition until his Nile campaign.

nodes.name: Regent Antipater & King Cassander of Macedon
nodes.role: Antipatrid Regents & Kings of Macedonia
sources: Henry Fynes Clinton, Fasti Hellenici Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Antipater governed Europe during Alexander's campaign; Cassander wed Thessalonike, sister of Alexander.

nodes.name: King Antigonus I Monophthalmus & Demetrius I Poliorcetes
nodes.role: Kings & Founders of the Antigonid Dynasty of Macedon
sources: Henry Fynes Clinton, Fasti Hellenici Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Master builders of Hellenistic siege warfare and progenitors of the Antigonid royal house until 168 BCE.

nodes.name: King Lysimachus of Thrace & Asia Minor
nodes.role: Bodyguard of Alexander & King of Thrace
sources: Quintus Curtius Rufus, History of Alexander the Great
Henry Fynes Clinton, Fasti Hellenici Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Wed Arsinoe II (daughter of Ptolemy I); defeated at Corupedion by Seleucus I in 281 BCE.

nodes.name: Eumenes of Cardia
nodes.role: Chief Royal Secretary & Champion of the Argead House
sources: Cornelius Nepos, Lives of Eminent Commanders (Watson 1853)
Quintus Curtius Rufus, History of Alexander the Great
nodes.notes: Greek secretary turned undefeated strategist in Asia Minor; profiled at length by Cornelius Nepos.

nodes.name: King Antiochus I Soter & Queen Stratonice
nodes.role: Second Seleucid King (of Half-Sogdian Descent)
sources: Henry Fynes Clinton, Fasti Hellenici Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Son of Seleucus I and Apama (daughter of Spitamenes); bridged Greco-Macedonian and Central Asian royalty.

nodes.name: Emperor Antiochus III 'the Great'
nodes.role: Seleucid Emperor & Restorer of the Eastern Anabasis
sources: Henry Fynes Clinton, Fasti Hellenici Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Led the Seleucid expedition through Parthia, Bactria, and the Kabul valley (212 - 205 BCE).

nodes.name: King Pyrrhus of Epirus
nodes.role: Aeacid King of Epirus & Maternal Cousin of Alexander
sources: Henry Fynes Clinton, Fasti Hellenici Vol. 1
Eutropius, Abridgment of Roman History (Watson 1853)
Aurelius Victor, Lives of the Illustrious Romans (1693)
Florus, Roman History (1675)
nodes.notes: Fought Rome at Heraclea and Asculum before returning to contest Macedon and Sparta.

nodes.name: King Demetrius I of Bactria & Eucratides I
nodes.role: Indo-Greek Kings of Bactria, Gandhara & Punjab
sources: Henry Fynes Clinton, Fasti Hellenici Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Expanded Hellenistic kingdoms across the Hindu Kush into northern India, preceding Menander I.

nodes.name: Vasudeva Anakadundubhi, Devaki & Rohini
nodes.role: Yadava Parents of Krishna, Balarama & Subhadra
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Detailed in Harivamsha Vishnu Parva: Vasudeva of the Shurasena clan wed Devaki and Rohini, linking Mathura and Hastinapura.

nodes.name: Prince Pradyumna of Dvaraka
nodes.role: Eldest Son of Krishna & Queen Rukmini; Vrishni Commander
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Harivamsha Vishnu Parva Chapters 99-109 relate Pradyumna's upbringing by Mayavati, slaying of Shambara, and defence of Dvaraka.

nodes.name: Prince Aniruddha & Princess Usha of Sonitapura
nodes.role: Son of Pradyumna & Daughter of King Banasura
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Krishna whose marriage to Usha unified the Vrishni house of Dvaraka with Sonitapura (Tezpur, Assam).

nodes.name: King Vajra (Vajranabha) of Indraprastha & Mathura
nodes.role: Great-Grandson of Krishna & King of Mathura
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Installed by Arjuna over Mathura/Indraprastha after the Mausala passing of Dvaraka, preserving the Yadava lineage.

nodes.name: Prince Samba, Son of Krishna & Jambavati
nodes.role: Vrishni Prince & Son-in-Law of Duryodhana
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Wed Lakshmana, daughter of Kuru king Duryodhana, in Harivamsha before later epic tragedies.

nodes.name: Satyaki (Yuyudhana) of the Vrishni Clan
nodes.role: Grandson of Sini & Pandava Charioteer Ally
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Disciple of Arjuna and undefeated Vrishni warrior across both Harivamsha and the Kurukshetra war.

nodes.name: Kritavarma of the Bhoja Clan
nodes.role: Son of Hridika & Commander of the Narayani Sena
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Bhoja Yadava general serving alongside Kuru forces while remaining kinsman to the Dvaraka house.

nodes.name: Akrura son of Shvaphalka
nodes.role: Vrishni Elder & Custodian of the Syamantaka Jewel
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Brought Krishna and Balarama from Vrindavana to Mathura; central figure in the Syamantaka cycle.

nodes.name: Uddhava (Pavanavyadhi) of Vrishni
nodes.role: Chief Counselor to Krishna & Cousin of the Yadavas
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Disciple of Brihaspati and recipient of Krishna's final discourse in epic and puranic tradition.

nodes.name: Queen Rukmini & King Rukmi of Vidarbha
nodes.role: Principal Queen of Dvaraka & King of Bhojakata
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Children of King Bhishmaka of Vidarbha; Rukmini wed Krishna while Rukmi founded Bhojakata.

nodes.name: Emperor Jarasandha of Magadha & King Sahadeva
nodes.role: Barhadratha Emperor of Girivraja (Rajagriha)
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Father-in-law of Kamsa whose eighteen sieges of Mathura prompted the Yadava migration to Dvaraka.

nodes.name: King Shishupala of Chedi & King Dantavakra
nodes.role: King of Chedi & Cousin of Krishna
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Chedi and Karusha monarchs allied to Jarasandha and challenged Krishna at Yudhishthira's Rajasuya.

nodes.name: King Kalayavana & Sage-King Muchukunda
nodes.role: Invader of Mathura & Ikshvaku Sovereign
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Harivamsha Vishnu Parva Ch. 57 narrates Krishna luring Kalayavana into Muchukunda's mountain cavern.

nodes.name: King Narakasura & King Bhagadatta of Pragjyotisha
nodes.role: Monarchs of Pragjyotisha / Kamarupa (Assam)
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Harivamsha details Naraka's defeat at Pragjyotisha and Krishna's installation of Bhagadatta as ally.

nodes.name: King Banasura of Sonitapura
nodes.role: Son of King Bali & Father-in-Law of Aniruddha
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Ruler of Sonitapura whose confrontation with Krishna ended in reconciliation through Usha and Aniruddha.

nodes.name: Paundraka Vasudeva & King of Kashi
nodes.role: Eastern Claimant & Sovereign of Varanasi
sources: Harivamsha (Prose English Translation, Vishnupurana & Bhavishyaparva)
nodes.notes: Harivamsha Bhavishya & Vishnu Parvas recount the war between Dvaraka and the Paundra-Kashi coalition.

nodes.name: Prince Siyamak & Shah Hushang
nodes.role: Son & Grandson of Gayomart; Pishdadian Shah
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Opening Pishdadian kings in Shahnameh Vol. 1 who instituted metalworking, irrigation, and the Sadeh festival.

nodes.name: Shah Tahmuras & Shah Jamshid
nodes.role: Pishdadian Monarchs; Founders of Writing, Silk & Nowruz
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Tahmuras the Demon-Binder taught script; Jamshid ordered society into four estates and founded Nowruz.

nodes.name: Shah Zahhak of the Serpents & Kaveh the Blacksmith
nodes.role: Tyrant Usurper & Champion of the Derafsh Kaviani Banner
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Kaveh raised his leather apron as Iran's royal standard to enthrone Fereydun against Zahhak.

nodes.name: Princes Salm, Tur & Iraj
nodes.role: Three Princes of Fereydun (Rum, Turan & Iran)
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Divided the world among Rum (Salm), Turan (Tur), and Iran (Iraj), sparking the multi-generational Irano-Turanian feud.

nodes.name: Paladins Nariman & Sam of Zabulistan
nodes.role: Hereditary Champions of Sistan & Father of Zal
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Ancestors of Rostam who guarded the eastern marches of Iran from Zabulistan under Manuchehr.

nodes.name: Princess Rudaba of Kabul & King Mihrab
nodes.role: Daughter of Kabuli King Mihrab & Mother of Rostam
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Descended through Sindukht and Mihrab; wed Zal and bore Rostam through the Simurgh's Caesarean counsel.

nodes.name: Princess Tahmina of Samangan
nodes.role: Princess of Samangan, Bride of Rostam & Mother of Sohrab
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Sent Sohrab with the onyx armlet of Rostam in one of the most famous tragedies of Shahnameh Vol. 1.

nodes.name: Faramarz & Banu Goshasp of Sistan
nodes.role: Son & Warrior-Daughter of Rostam
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Heroic children of Rostam who led campaigns in India and upheld the house of Sam.

nodes.name: Shah Kay Qobad
nodes.role: Founder & First Shah of the Kayanian Dynasty
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Descendant of Manuchehr fetched from Mount Alborz by young Rostam to restore the Iranian throne.

nodes.name: Shah Kay Kavus
nodes.role: Kayanian Shah; Sovereign of Mazandaran & Hamavaran Wars
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Father of Siyavash and grandfather of Kay Khosrow in Shahnameh.

nodes.name: Prince Siyavash & Princess Farangis
nodes.role: Kayanian Crown Prince & Turanian Royal Bride
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Passed the ordeal of fire, built Siyavashgerd, wed Afrasiyab's daughter Farangis, and fathered Kay Khosrow.

nodes.name: King Afrasiyab of Turan
nodes.role: Descendant of Tur & Sovereign of Turan
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Heir of Tur son of Fereydun; grandfather of Kay Khosrow through Princess Farangis.

nodes.name: Heroes Tus, Gudarz & Giv
nodes.role: Generals of Iran & Rescuers of Kay Khosrow
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Tus son of Nowzar and Giv son of Gudarz rescued young Kay Khosrow from Turan across the Oxus.

nodes.name: Shahs Lohrasp, Goshtasp & Prince Esfandiyar
nodes.role: Kayanian Shahs & Royal Patrons of Zoroaster
sources: Firdausi, The Shahnama of Firdausi Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Succeeded Kay Khosrow as designated heir, embraced the Avestan revelation of Zoroaster, and fought Rostam.

nodes.name: Pope Clement I of Rome & Abdias of Babylon
nodes.role: Disciple of Peter & Compiler of Apostolic Acts
sources: Abdias of Babylon, The Apostolical History
nodes.notes: Abdias is styled bishop of Babylon appointed by Simon and Jude; Clement transmits early Roman succession.

nodes.name: Bishops Linus & Anacletus (Cletus) of Rome
nodes.role: Immediate Roman Episcopal Successors of Peter
sources: Abdias of Babylon, The Apostolical History
nodes.notes: Early episcopal list linking Peter's Roman ministry to late first-century Rome.

nodes.name: St. Petronilla of Rome
nodes.role: Spiritual / Traditional Daughter of Apostle Peter
sources: Abdias of Babylon, The Apostolical History
nodes.notes: Venerated in the Catacomb of Domitilla and profiled in Abdias's Petrine cycle.

nodes.name: King Gondophares & Gad of Indo-Parthia
nodes.role: Indo-Parthian King of Taxila in the Acts of Thomas
sources: Abdias of Babylon, The Apostolical History
nodes.notes: Numismatically attested Parthian monarch featured in Abdias Book IX's mission of St. Thomas.

nodes.name: King Misdaeus (Mazdai) & Queen Mygdonia
nodes.role: Indian King & Queen in the Martyrdom of Thomas
sources: Abdias of Babylon, The Apostolical History
nodes.notes: Abdias Book IX places St. Thomas's final royal ministry in the household of King Misdaeus and Vizan.

nodes.name: King Polymius & Astyages of India/Armenia
nodes.role: Royal Brothers in the Bartholomew Cycle
sources: Abdias of Babylon, The Apostolical History
nodes.notes: Abdias Book VIII recounts King Polymius's conversion before his brother Astyages arrested Bartholomew.

nodes.name: King Egippus, Hirtacus & Princess Ephigenia of Ethiopia
nodes.role: Nubian-Ethiopian Royal Converts of St. Matthew
sources: Abdias of Babylon, The Apostolical History
nodes.notes: Abdias Book VII sets Matthew's mission in Nadaber among King Egippus, Candace's realm, and Princess Ephigenia.

nodes.name: King Xerxes of Babylon & Persian Governors
nodes.role: Mesopotamian Rulers in the Acts of Simon & Jude
sources: Abdias of Babylon, The Apostolical History
nodes.notes: Abdias Book VI links Apostles Simon the Zealot and Jude Thaddeus to royal courts between Edessa and Babylon.

nodes.name: Drusiana & Aristodemus of Ephesus
nodes.role: Ephesian Matron & Temple Priest in the Acts of John
sources: Abdias of Babylon, The Apostolical History
nodes.notes: Abdias Book V links the Johannine circle at Ephesus to Domitian's Rome and Patmos.

nodes.name: Sextus Julius Africanus of Emmaus
nodes.role: Christian Chronographer & Envoy to Elagabalus
sources: Ante-Nicene Fathers Vol. 6 (Julius Africanus, Gregory Thaumaturgus, Dionysius, Arnobius, Lactantius)
nodes.notes: Author of Chronographiai (ANF Vol. 6), harmonizing the Desposyni genealogies of Jesus with Greek Olympiads and Egyptian dynasties.

nodes.name: Gregory Thaumaturgus of Neocaesarea
nodes.role: Bishop of Pontus & Disciple of Origen
sources: Ante-Nicene Fathers Vol. 6 (Julius Africanus, Gregory Thaumaturgus, Dionysius, Arnobius, Lactantius)
nodes.notes: Pontic aristocrat and canonical writer in ANF Vol. 6 who evangelized Cappadocia and Pontus.

nodes.name: Pope Dionysius the Great of Alexandria
nodes.role: Patriarch of Alexandria & Scholar of Revelation
sources: Ante-Nicene Fathers Vol. 6 (Julius Africanus, Gregory Thaumaturgus, Dionysius, Arnobius, Lactantius)
nodes.notes: Corresponded with Rome, Antioch, and Nepos in Egypt; preserved key third-century Alexandrian history in ANF Vol. 6.

nodes.name: Methodius of Olympus & Patara
nodes.role: Lycian Bishop & Author of the Symposium
sources: Ante-Nicene Fathers Vol. 6 (Julius Africanus, Gregory Thaumaturgus, Dionysius, Arnobius, Lactantius)
nodes.notes: Critiqued Origen's cosmology in Lycia; excerpted in ANF Vol. 6 before his martyrdom under Maximinus.

nodes.name: Arnobius of Sicca Veneria
nodes.role: African Rhetorician & Teacher of Lactantius
sources: Ante-Nicene Fathers Vol. 6 (Julius Africanus, Gregory Thaumaturgus, Dionysius, Arnobius, Lactantius)
nodes.notes: Wrote Seven Books Against the Heathen in Numidia; mentor to Lactantius in ANF Vol. 6.

nodes.name: Lactantius (Lucius Caecilius Firmianus)
nodes.role: Christian Cicero & Tutor to Crispus son of Constantine
sources: Ante-Nicene Fathers Vol. 6 (Julius Africanus, Gregory Thaumaturgus, Dionysius, Arnobius, Lactantius)
nodes.notes: Taught at Diocletian's Nicomedia before tutoring Constantine I's eldest son Crispus at Trier (ANF Vol. 6).

nodes.name: St. Pamphilus of Caesarea & Pierius
nodes.role: Founder of the Library of Caesarea & Mentor of Eusebius
sources: Ante-Nicene Fathers Vol. 6 (Julius Africanus, Gregory Thaumaturgus, Dionysius, Arnobius, Lactantius)
nodes.notes: Preserved Origen's Hexapla and Julius Africanus's manuscripts for Eusebius of Caesarea.

nodes.name: Sargon & Naram-Sin of Agade (Chronicle of Early Kings)
nodes.role: Akkadian Kings in Neo-Babylonian Chronicles
sources: L.W. King, Chronicles Concerning Early Babylonian Kings Vol. 1
nodes.notes: L.W. King Vol. 1 edits the Neo-Babylonian Chronicle of Early Kings recounting Sargon's Westland crossing and Naram-Sin's Magan expedition.

nodes.name: Kings Shulgi, Amar-Sin & Ibbi-Sin of Ur III
nodes.role: Third Dynasty of Ur Kings in the Weidner / King Chronicles
sources: L.W. King, Chronicles Concerning Early Babylonian Kings Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Linked to Marduk temple cult traditions in L.W. King's Chronicle of Early Kings.

nodes.name: Kings Ilushuma & Puzur-Ashur I of Assyria
nodes.role: Old Assyrian Kings & Synchronism with Su-abu of Babylon
sources: L.W. King, Chronicles Concerning Early Babylonian Kings Vol. 1
nodes.notes: L.W. King documents Ilushuma's synchronism with Su-abu/Sumu-abum of Babylon, anchoring early Mesopotamian chronology.

nodes.name: King Ulamburiash & Ea-gamil of the Sealand
nodes.role: Kassite King & Conqueror of the First Sealand Dynasty
sources: L.W. King, Chronicles Concerning Early Babylonian Kings Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Brother of Kashtiliash III; ended the southern Sealand dynasty of Ea-gamil as preserved in L.W. King's Chronicle.

nodes.name: Kings Karaindash & Kurigalzu I of Karduniash
nodes.role: Kassite Kings, Builders of Dur-Kurigalzu & Amarna Correspondents
sources: L.W. King, Chronicles Concerning Early Babylonian Kings Vol. 1
A.H. Sayce, The Races of the Old Testament
Records of the Past Vol. 9 (Sayce ed.)
nodes.notes: Established diplomatic brotherhood with Egypt (Amenhotep III) and treaty frontiers with Ashur-bel-nisheshu.

nodes.name: Kings Nazibugash & Kurigalzu II of Babylon
nodes.role: Kassite Kings in the Synchronistic Chronicle
sources: L.W. King, Chronicles Concerning Early Babylonian Kings Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Enthroned following Ashur-uballit I's intervention after the assassination of Burnaburiash II's grandson.

nodes.name: King Adad-nirari III & Queen Sammuramat
nodes.role: Neo-Assyrian King & Queen Mother; Overlord of Damascus
sources: A.H. Sayce, The Races of the Old Testament
Records of the Past Vol. 9 (Sayce ed.)
nodes.notes: Exact contemporary of Ben-hadad III and Jehoash of Israel; profiled in Sayce's Records of the Past.

nodes.name: King Marduk-apla-iddina II (Merodach-Baladan)
nodes.role: Chaldean King of Babylon & Ally of Hezekiah
sources: L.W. King, Chronicles Concerning Early Babylonian Kings Vol. 1
A.H. Sayce, The Races of the Old Testament
Records of the Past Vol. 9 (Sayce ed.)
nodes.notes: Contested Babylon repeatedly against Sargon II and Sennacherib; sent envoys to Jerusalem (2 Kings 20 / Isaiah 39).

nodes.name: King Kandalanu of Babylon
nodes.role: Vassal King of Babylon Prior to Nabopolassar
sources: L.W. King, Chronicles Concerning Early Babylonian Kings Vol. 1
nodes.notes: Twenty-one-year reign bridging late Assyrian hegemony and Nabopolassar's Neo-Babylonian accession.

nodes.name: Syro-Hittite & Kheta Lineage (Sayce Ethnology)
nodes.role: Canaanite-Hamitic / Anatolian Synthesis in Sayce
sources: A.H. Sayce, The Races of the Old Testament
Records of the Past Vol. 9 (Sayce ed.)
nodes.notes: A.H. Sayce maps Egyptian Kheta, Assyrian Khatti, and biblical Heth/Canaan across northern Syria and Anatolia.

nodes.name: Elamite Anzanite & Susiana Line (Sayce Ethnology)
nodes.role: Highland Elam & Susa Ethnic Stratum
sources: A.H. Sayce, The Races of the Old Testament
Records of the Past Vol. 9 (Sayce ed.)
nodes.notes: Sayce contrasts Semitic-speaking Asshur and Aram with Turanian/Anzanite Susa under Genesis 10's geographical framework.

nodes.name: Kittim, Alashiya & Javan Aegean Stratum (Sayce)
nodes.role: Cypriot-Ionian Maritime Lineage under Japheth
sources: A.H. Sayce, The Races of the Old Testament
Records of the Past Vol. 9 (Sayce ed.)
nodes.notes: Tracks Javan (Yavana/Ionian), Elishah (Alashiya), and Kittim (Kition in Cyprus) in Sayce's Races of the Old Testament.

nodes.name: Crawford's Patriarchal Dynasties Canon (1877)
nodes.role: Dynastic-Age Interpretation of Antediluvian & Postdiluvian Eras
sources: T.P. Crawford, The Patriarchal Dynasties from Adam to Abraham
nodes.notes: T.P. Crawford argued Genesis 5 & 11 patrilineages record both personal reigns and dynastic house spans bridging Noah to Abraham.

nodes.name: Father Louis Hennepin (Recollect Chronicler)
nodes.role: Chronicler of Niagara Falls, Lake Superior & the Upper Mississippi
sources: Louis Hennepin, A New Discovery of a Vast Country in America (1699)
nodes.notes: Flemish Franciscan explorer under La Salle who published the 1697/1699 London edition dedicated to William III and Louis XIV's frontier.

nodes.name: Rene-Robert Cavelier de La Salle & Great Lakes Sachems
nodes.role: French Royal Explorer & Franco-Iroquois/Sioux Diplomatic Contact
sources: Louis Hennepin, A New Discovery of a Vast Country in America (1699)
nodes.notes: Led the Griffon expedition with Hennepin and claimed Louisiana for Louis XIV, recording Dakota, Illinois, and Iroquois councils.

edges.label: Tutor of Crispus son of Constantine
